title: Federal pump-at-work rights
facts: The FLSA as amended by the PUMP Act generally requires covered employers to provide reasonable break time for an employee to express breast milk for a nursing child for one year after the child's birth.
Employers generally must provide a place to pump that is shielded from view, free from intrusion and not a bathroom.
Whether pumping time must be paid depends on circumstances, including whether the employee is completely relieved from duty and whether other paid-break rules apply.
An employer with fewer than 50 employees may invoke a statutory undue-hardship exemption only when the legal requirements for that exemption are met.
